order_description: Implantation of a hypoglossal nerve neurostimulator system (stimulation lead, pulse generator and respiratory sensor) for obstructive sleep apnea

candidates.title: Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea
Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea
Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea

selection_reason: All three candidates are the same Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation for Obstructive Sleep Apnea policy from different contractors, and it governs the order for implanting a hypoglossal nerve stimulator for OSA. The patient's 2026-08-31 sleep study shows AHI 14/h (mild OSA), which appears to fall below the typical AHI threshold of 15 in this policy, so coverage criteria may not be met. Pick L38398 as the governing policy; the contractor version does not change the choice.

criteria.policy_text: Beneficiary is 22 years of age or older
criteria.explanation: The patient is documented as 69 years old in the 2026-06-26 and 2026-09-05 notes, well above 22.

criteria.policy_text: Body mass index (BMI) is less than 35 kg/m2
criteria.explanation: BMI is recorded as 27.86 kg/m2 on 2025-06-20 and 2026-06-26. The 2026-08-18 note records 33.0 kg/m2, which is also under 35.

criteria.policy_text: A polysomnography (PSG) is performed within 24 months of first consultation for HGNS implant
criteria.explanation: The first documented sleep apnea consultation was 2026-08-18, and the in-laboratory PSG was completed 2026-08-30. No separate HGNS implant consultation is recorded, so the earliest sleep visit is used and the PSG falls well within 24 months.

criteria.policy_text: Beneficiary has predominantly obstructive events (defined as central and mixed apneas less than 25% of the total AHI)
criteria.explanation: The PSG report describes mild obstructive sleep apnea with 91 total events, but it does not give the number or percentage of central and mixed apneas, so the less than 25 percent threshold cannot be verified.

criteria.policy_text: AHI is 15 to 65 events per hour
criteria.explanation: The AHI is recorded as 14 per hour on 2026-08-31 and in the PSG report, which is below the required minimum of 15.

criteria.policy_text: Documentation demonstrates CPAP failure (AHI greater than 15 despite CPAP usage) or CPAP intolerance (less than 4 hours per night, 5 nights per week, or CPAP returned), including shared decision making that the patient was intolerant of CPAP despite consultation with a sleep expert
criteria.explanation: CPAP was ordered on 2026-09-05 and user instruction was given on 2026-09-11, but no CPAP usage, CPAP failure, CPAP return, or shared decision making conversation about CPAP intolerance is documented.

criteria.policy_text: Absence of complete concentric collapse at the soft palate level as seen on a drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) procedure
criteria.explanation: No drug-induced sleep endoscopy is documented in the record.

criteria.policy_text: No other anatomical findings that would compromise performance of device (e.g., tonsil size 3 or 4 per standardized tonsillar hypertrophy grading scale)
criteria.explanation: Mallampati class IV and neck circumference of 17 inches are recorded, but tonsil size and other anatomical findings relevant to device performance are not documented.

criteria.policy_text: HGNS is not reasonable and necessary when contraindications are present, including central and mixed apneas making up more than one-quarter of AHI, an implantable device that could interact with the system, BMI of 35 or more, neuromuscular disease, hypoglossal nerve palsy, severe pulmonary disease, cardiac conditions, and others
criteria.explanation: The documented BMI does not reach 35, and no listed contraindication is recorded. However, the central and mixed apnea proportion, implanted device status, neuromuscular disease, hypoglossal nerve palsy, pulmonary and cardiac conditions are not documented either way.

decision_explanation: Covered Indications.5 is not met because the AHI is 14 events per hour, below the required 15 to 65 range. Because the policy requires all listed criteria to be met, the order is denied regardless of the criteria that remain insufficient in the record.
